page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2500 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the i7ie.xlarge demonstrates strong single-core performance, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2314.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (34.74 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.0 GB/sec). Multi-core performance is more moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 4390.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5145.0, both falling into the average to weak categories. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read performance at 34.18 GB/sec for large blocks, but average write performance at 36.32 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput are average, with the latter reaching 8.21 GB/sec.

The qualitative value of the i7ie.xlarge lies in its high local storage density and DDR5 memory capacity relative to its 4 vCPUs. While multi-core compute and memory read bandwidth are limited, the combination of a 2500 GB NVMe SSD and 32 GB of RAM makes it highly resource-dense for storage-heavy workloads. This server is best suited for local databases, caching layers, data-intensive applications requiring fast local scratch space, and workloads that benefit from strong single-threaded CPU performance and hardware-accelerated matrix operations.
